need: Find out where a research idea stands and what to do next
why: Reads the idea's folder and names the one thing to run now, so nothing gets skipped or done twice.

need: Turn what I believe about a new idea into first models
why: One short interview about your beliefs, then proto personas, journeys and jobs, each marked as an assumption, and the belief to test first.

need: Plan interviews
why: Asks about what people did, not what they would do, and ties every question to a belief it can confirm or break.

need: Make personas from real interviews

rival.why: writes a fluent persona whether or not anyone was interviewed

why: Real mode needs five people from different organisations and links every line to the passage it came from.

need: Map a journey

rival.why: does not separate what you believe from what you saw

why: Current or future journey, with each step marked as belief or evidence.

need: Sort research notes into themes
why: Sorts from the bottom up, counts people rather than notes, and has a second agent re-sort blind to check the themes hold.

need: Plan a usability test
why: Tasks, success measures and sample size, tied to the belief the test is meant to settle.

need: Blueprint the service behind the screens
why: Seven lanes per step, checked by script, from research rather than from guesswork.

need: Work out why people can't find things
why: My most used IA skill. It traces each path a person would take and names where it breaks.

need: Decide the page tree for a site

rival.why: writes the sitemap as a file for wireframes to build on, once the structure is decided

why: Places every page, checks the tree agrees with itself and scales to the job.

need: Plan or restructure a public website
why: Pages, URLs, header, footer and links that lead a visitor to a decision. Beat the skill it replaced 31 to 26 of 32 checks.

need: Design navigation
why: Works from the content and the tasks, not from a list of menu patterns.

need: Set URL rules or plan redirects

rival.why: is the one to use once URLs are moving

why: Rules a whole site can follow, with a script that checks a list of URLs against them.

need: Test a structure before building it
why: Plans the tasks and reads the results of a tree test, so the labels are tested before the screens.

need: Design a form

rival.why: is the first step of design-form, which then adds passes on choice load, memory, targets, errors, feedback and loading

why: Structure, chunking, validation, errors and completion in one run.

need: Map a component's states

rival.why: models the states but skips the loading, error and feedback passes map-states adds

why: States, events, guards and edge cases, then what each state looks like.

need: Design what happens when something fails

rival.why: covers messages; error-flow also covers prevention and recovery paths

why: Prevention, detection, messaging and recovery.

need: Design a first-run experience
why: The activation path, what to reveal when, and time to first value.

need: Design the wait

rival.why: is for confirming an action, not for waiting on one

why: Spinners, skeletons, optimistic updates and progressive reveal.

need: Tell people an action registered

rival.why: is for waiting, not for confirming

why: Confirmations, status changes and notifications.

need: Tune how one animation feels
why: My most used MC Dean skill: easing, staging and follow-through for one specific motion.

need: Draw a flow before any screens exist

rival.why: draws a standalone diagram; the Design OS flow is a file the screen inventory and wireframes must agree with

why: Includes what happens when the task goes wrong, and a script fails if a later stage drops a step.

need: List every screen a feature needs
why: Each screen with its loading, empty, error and permission states, checked against the flow.

need: Wireframe a feature
why: Greyscale screens as files the next stages read. Plain Claude draws well already; the value is that the chain is checked.

need: A clickable prototype to test a flow
why: Built from the wireframes, so every arrow in the flow is clickable or the check fails.

need: A quick throwaway build to feel something out
why: Built to be thrown away, which keeps it fast.

need: Design or rebuild a landing page
why: From a brief to a built page, with critic passes before it calls itself done.

need: Polish one section to a high bar
why: Section-level craft with its own reviewers.

need: Critique a page against our own rules

rival.why: critiques against general principles rather than the project's written rules

why: Every issue quotes a rule from taste.md or DESIGN.md word for word, so the critique can't drift into taste.

need: Write interface copy

rival.why: covers the same ground; pick one and keep it

why: Microcopy, error messages, empty states and calls to action.

need: Plan content: what exists, who owns it, what to make
why: A content strategy as the finished document, with the working notes kept apart.

need: Make AI-written text sound human
why: Checks text against a public catalogue of the signs of AI writing.

need: Tighten and proofread copy
why: Several focused sweeps rather than one rewrite.

need: Check UI against the design system while building
why: My most used tool by far. Names the component to use and flags hardcoded values.

need: Start a design system from a live website
why: Measures the site's real styles across pages and records where every value came from.

need: Choose a visual direction before tokens exist
why: Two or three directions to pick between, written down so the next stage can build from the pick.

need: Change a token's value
why: Even the one-line changes, so nothing downstream breaks quietly.

need: Rename or remove a token or component
why: Ships a codemod, not a find and replace.

need: Audit an existing design system

rival.why: hands each step to another skill in its pack, and nothing checks the report it writes

why: Holds the system to its own written rules, quotes the line behind every finding, and a gate opens each one.

need: Write a design brief
why: The brief is the finished document, in plain words, with the scoring kept in a working file.

need: Set a north star
why: One direction the team can test decisions against.

need: Size up competitors
why: What each one does about the job, not a feature grid.

need: Personas that include disability and situational limits
why: Starts with who is being left out, before the design is fixed.

need: Set up a new project's files
why: Nine annotated templates, each saying what the file is for and who reads it. Writes only what is missing and asks three questions at most.

need: Iterate a Workshopr page to a quality bar
why: Designs, then an independent critic scores each pass, and it loops until the bar is met.

need: Plan a new feature before building it
why: Looks everything up, asks one question at a time and writes a spec, a design brief and build slices.

need: Build a planned feature slice
why: An independent reviewer scores every pass, and a gate holds it until tests, lint and the design system pass.

need: Run someone else's skill and keep its claims honest
why: Runs a third-party skill unedited, files its claims as belief or evidence, and an auditor checks the citations.
